attempts.summary: Built an Ansible playbook run from control_node node4 that makes node1 (VyOS) the DNS resolver for the shared private network 10.100.66.0/24: node1 answers inventory.internal with node2's address (10.100.66.11) via a VyOS static-host-mapping (consumed by pdns-recursor's default hosts-file lookup) and forwards everything else upstream via VyOS's DHCP-learned system nameserver. node2 and node3 were configured via community.general.nmcli to use node1 (10.100.66.10) as their resolver, overriding DHCP-provided DNS. The playbook is idempotent and self-verifying (dig/getent checks with assertions). Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart evidence protocol for all four nodes, proving each reboot via a changed OS boot_id and confirming DNS/config recovery afterward.
